observed_anchor: PR #744 adds a path-only String process hostcall through the single ClayVM and records HostProcessReceipt.argv, but requested path identity is not necessarily executed binary identity.
hypothesis: A path/argv receipt is sufficient to bind the executed program identity for the path-only String process effect.
counterhypothesis: The same absolute path string can resolve to a different executable between invocations, so a path/argv receipt proves request/outcome but not stable executed binary identity.

experiment.name: EXECUTABLE_SYMLINK_RETARGET_SAME_PATH
experiment.evidence_scope: source-equivalent reconstruction of current-main claymachine/host_process.py behavior; NOT exact Git-blob execution and NOT EntityOS artifact execution
experiment.baseline: One absolute symlink path pointed to /usr/bin/true and run_host_process((path,)) returned rc=0.
experiment.intervention: The same symlink path was retargeted to /usr/bin/false and run_host_process((same_path,)) returned rc=1.
experiment.observation: Both receipts retained the same argv path string while process behavior changed from rc=0 to rc=1.

test_obligation: Before provenance-strong promotion of linux.process.spawn.path.v1, explicitly choose and test receipt scope: either bind post-spawn executable identity, bind/open an executable descriptor under a declared identity policy, or state that v1 receipts are path/outcome receipts and keep executed-binary identity OPEN.
next_executable_step: Apply the receipt-scope decision to retained PR #744 and replay it on the exact PR head in an actually-started isolated/source-admitted full-repository sandbox together with existing CM-TERM/single-VM/strict-ClayOS gates and an exact one-file EntityOS rebuild/self-test.
